title: fix(rest)!: PUT and the five by-name /meta sub-doors declare closed query sets, so ?member= is refused, never dropped (#23072, RestServer half)
body:
Part of #23072
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

This is the `RestServer` half of #23072. `PUT /meta/:type/:name` and the five by-name sub-doors outside ruling 6116165299's list (`/references`, `/layers`, `/audit`, `/diff`, `/published`) now each declare a closed query-parameter set (AGENTS.md route rule 5). So the bundle member selector `?member=`, and any other name a door does not read, gets a located `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` instead of being dropped.

**#23072 remains open for the other half: the runtime dispatcher's `/meta` item GET.** That half needs `META_ITEM_READ_PARAMS` and the refusal sentence from `@objectstack/rest`. Neither is on the package's published entry, so reaching them needs a NEW public export. The dispatch reserved that decision, so the half goes back to the seat as `needs_decision`, with the measurement below. No dispatcher code is in this PR.

## Patch round 1: the changeset declares the narrowing (new head `d64fc8e605`)

The contract review of `d813364338` (`6138381862`) failed on ② only. The changeset graded six doors' accept-set narrowing `patch`, under a bare `Clause-②: no` and with no ADR-0087 disposition, so every gate read it as non-breaking. This round edits `.changeset/23072-meta-doors-closed-sets.md` only (commit `49994b3335`), then merges `origin/main` (merge commit `d64fc8e605`, the new head). No source file moves, and the merge brought nothing under `packages/rest`.

- `'@objectstack/rest': minor` (was `patch`).
- The summary line is `fix(rest)!: …`, and this PR's title carries the same `!`.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (was `Clause-②: no`), in the changeset and on line 2 above.
- Exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker, in the HTML-comment form: `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Its facts, each checked against the diff:
  - No path under `packages/spec`, no metadata schema and no stored shape is in the diff.
  - The six closed sets are module constants that `packages/rest/src/index.ts` does not re-export. The build entry is `src/index.ts` alone, and `exports` holds only `.`.
  - The one removed source line is inside `unknownQueryParamMessage`, which the entry does not export either.
  - The diff names no ADR-0087 id, and `@objectstack/rest` publishes.
- The launch-window banner, `**BREAKING** (an accept-set narrowing)`, shipped as `minor`.
- The per-door remedies stay as written.

Gates at `d64fc8e605`, each exit captured before any pipe:

- `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main`: exit 0, `check-adr-0087-registration: 1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition.` The signals read are `BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing`, and the disposition is `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main`: exit 0, `This diff introduces no major bump.` Locally the level axis reads NOT APPLICABLE, because there is no `pull_request` payload. Driven offline with `--event` carrying this title and body: exit 0, `LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② no (narrowing), and no package whose published source … it moves is graded patch.` Control, the same body against the old head `d813364338`, whose changeset still says `patch`: exit 1, `clause-② declares no (narrowing) while no moved package is graded minor or above`. So line 2 and the changeset have to move together, and at `d64fc8e605` they do.
- `node scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs --base origin/main`: exit 0.
- `pnpm check:changeset-gate-self-tests`: exit 0 (170, 548 and 401 assertions).
- `dispatch-gates --commands` with no paths, at `d64fc8e605`: 65 commands over 5 paths against merge base `dc93781c1`, and all 65 exit 0. On the first pass `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: a fresh worktree has no `dist/`). After `turbo run build --filter='!@objectstack/docs' --concurrency=2` through the lock (`74 successful`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`) all three exit 0. `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` had run while that build was still writing, so it was re-run on the finished build: exit 0. `dispatch-gates --ran`: `65 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`.
- `origin/main` moved to `e540e7ffb9` during the run, 5 commits, none under `packages/rest` and none in the changeset gates. The same derivation over this PR's 5 paths, on a throwaway checkout of `e540e7ffb9`, gives the identical 65 commands.
- The `@objectstack/rest` tests were not re-run: the merge brought no change under `packages/rest`, and this round moves no source file.

## The defect, per door

None of the six declared a set. Each read the names it knew and ignored the rest. `PUT /meta/email_template/x?member=zh-CN` with an `en-US` body wrote `en-US` and answered `200`. The five GETs answered for the canonical member a request that named another. Both are plausible answers about the wrong row, and no status, header or field told them apart.

## The sets, measured from each handler's read points

All six live in `registerMetadataEndpointsInner`, on base `bcebd8409d`. Each door's helpers were read too, not just the handler body. The whole-request helpers `resolveExecCtx`, `resolveProtocol` (route, hostname, `X-Environment-Id`), `resolveObjectMasker`, `resolveMetadataService`, `walledCatalogRefusal`, `resolveMetaWriteActor` and the read-gate sources read no query key. The cloud host's `kernel-resolver` strategy is not in this tree, so it was not read.

| door | read points | before | after (exported beside `META_ITEM_*_PARAMS`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PUT /meta/:type/:name` | `force` (handler), `package` (`metaItemPackageBinding`), `mode` (a frame down, `metaSaveRequestOptions`, `meta-save-request.ts:118`) | none | `META_ITEM_SAVE_PARAMS` = `force`, `package`, `mode` |
| `GET …/references` | none | none | `META_ITEM_REFERENCES_PARAMS` = (empty) |
| `GET …/layers` | `package` (a frame down, `serveMetaItemLayered`) | none | `META_ITEM_LAYERS_PARAMS` = `package` |
| `GET …/audit` | `limit` (`readDeclaredQueryNumber`) | none | `META_ITEM_AUDIT_PARAMS` = `limit` |
| `GET …/diff` | `from`, `to`, `fromVersion`, `toVersion` (`readDeclaredQueryNumber`) | none | `META_ITEM_DIFF_PARAMS` = those four |
| `GET …/published` | none | none | `META_ITEM_PUBLISHED_PARAMS` = (empty) |

`PUT`, `/audit` and `/diff` already had a multiplicity guard over exactly these names. Recognition runs just before it, after the capability and authoring gates, which is the placement the five ruled doors use. `/references`, `/layers` and `/published` open with recognition, as the item GET does. The refusal is the file's own `refuseUnknownQueryParams`, which writes the nested envelope `{ error: { code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message } }`. That is the envelope the five ruled doors answer for a name they do not know.

`PUT` stays body-addressed (ruling 6116165299): it refuses `member` and does not read it. None of the five sub-doors starts honouring `member`, because their protocol requests do not declare it. They refuse it.

## One edit outside the claimed file surface: `query-allowlist.ts`

`/references` and `/published` read no query parameter, so their closed sets are empty. They are the first empty sets in the repository. With an empty set, `unknownQueryParamMessage` ended `Supported parameters: .`, which reads as a truncated answer and would have shipped with this PR. The function now ends `This endpoint takes no query parameters.` when the set is empty. Every non-empty set's sentence is byte-identical to before: the three existing pins of that message (`rest-server-approvals-unknown-filter.test.ts`, `rest-server-closed-query-params.test.ts`, `rest-server-meta-member-selector.test.ts`) pass unchanged. This file is not in the claim's file surface. It is declared here, and in the report to the seat, rather than worked around with a second refusal dialect.

## Caller census: every in-repo caller of these doors, and what it sends

| caller | sends | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/client` `meta.saveItem` (both clients, one `metaSaveQuery` builder) | `force`, `package`, `mode` | green |
| `@objectstack/client` `getReferences` / `getPublished` | nothing | green |
| `@objectstack/client` `getAudit` / `diffItem` | `limit` / `from`, `to` | green |
| objectui at the pin `1fb1ced36243`, `@object-ui/data-objectstack` `MetadataClient` (`save`, `layered`, `references`, `diff`, `audit`), shallow-fetched read-only | `force`, `mode`, `package` / `package` / nothing / `from`, `to` / `limit`; no `/published` caller | green |
| objectui `UnpublishedAppBar.tsx`, `metadata-admin/external/api.ts` (`PUT` by `fetch`) | no query | green |
| dogfood: 9 files `PUT` with a query string | `package` ×21, `mode` ×16, `force` ×1 | green, measured below |
| dogfood: the 7 `/layers` and `/published` callers | no query | green, measured below |
| `packages/rest/src/meta-item-save-capability-gate.test.ts` "query/body-smuggled organization ids" | `?organizationId=` on `PUT`, a name the door never read | **inert. Red under the new set; fixed here** |

The one inert caller is a test pin written while `PUT` dropped unknown names: it asserted that a query-smuggled `organizationId` "does not reach the write" by watching it get dropped. It is split in two. The body half is unchanged: `200`, and `organizationId` is not in the save request. The query half is now the located `400`, with `saveMetaItem` never called. That is the same invariant, made loud. No SDK or console caller sends a name outside a new set, so the census found no `needs_decision`.

## Not here: the runtime dispatcher's `/meta` item GET

Measured on `bcebd8409d`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` `handleMetadataRequest`:

- **Read points:** `state`, `preview`, `package`, `layers` (`wantsMetaItemLayers`) and `locale` (`metaRequestLocale`, inside `createMetaItemAnswer`). `member` is never read and never forwarded.
- **One source for the set:** `@objectstack/runtime` imports from `@objectstack/rest` (a single `.` export). Its index exports `metaItemPackageBinding`, `metaSaveRequestOptions`, `repeatedQueryParamMessage` and the read-gate family. It does not export `META_ITEM_READ_PARAMS`, `META_ITEM_MEMBER_PARAM`, `metaMemberSelector`, `refuseUnknownQueryParams` or `unknownQueryParamMessage`. Reaching any of them needs a new public export, so this PR stops there.
- **The envelope:** `RestServer` writes `{ error: { code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message } }`. The dispatcher's `deps.error(message, 400)` writes `{ success: false, error: { code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message, … } }` through `buildApiError`. The `rest` index already records that split for the multiplicity rule ("a dispatcher domain takes the message and builds its own body"). So "the same envelope" means the same `error.code` and the same message, each in its own transport's body.
- **What honouring `member` costs there, beyond the export:** three `getMetaItem` calls need it (the `object` branch, the generic branch and `readPendingDraft`). Two lookups wrap `getMetaItem` in a bare `catch {}`, which would swallow the protocol's located `400` for a bad selector and fall through to the registry or `MetadataService`. The `MetadataService` fallback (`getItem(type, name, packageId)`) keys by name alone, so for a member the protocol answers absent it would serve the canonical member. The `?layers=` with `member` refusal is a sentence in `rest-server.ts` too.

The options and their analysis are in the report on #23072.

## For the spec lane: could PR #23070's reader serve `member` on the five sub-doors?

This is read from source, not built. `resolveBundleMemberSelector` resolves the selector on every door. What differs is whether the door's store can address a member:

- **`/references`: no, permanently.** `findReferencesToMeta` sweeps the graph for items that name `(type, name)`. A reference names an item, not one member of a bundle, so there is nothing to select. The refusal is the right answer, not a gap.
- **`/layers`: yes, with threading.** The overlay read `findServedOverlayRow` already takes `member`, and so do the code reads `lookupArtifactItem` and `registry.getItem`. `getMetaItemLayered` passes none. The `MetadataService` code read (`readItemFromMetadataService`) would need the addressed-member check `getMetaItem` applies. `overlayLockLayerAt` reads every member's rows by name. `GetMetaItemLayeredRequestSchema` would need the field.
- **`/audit`: no, not with the reader alone.** `sys_metadata_audit` has no member column (`type`, `name`, `organization_id`, `operation`, …), so every member's attempts share one trail. Serving `member` needs a column, the writer stamping it, and `AuditMetaItemRequestSchema.member`.
- **`/diff`: yes, with threading.** `historyRowsOfMember(type, rows, member)` already takes a member, and `diffMetaItem` passes none. The default `to` (the active version) would read a member-scoped active row, and `RestServer`'s per-caller gate reads the canonical current document (`fetchCurrentMetaDocument`). No spec request is declared for the door.
- **`/published`: partly.** The overlay half rides `getMetaItemLayered`, as `/layers` does. The code and package snapshot fallback `getPublished` reads `MetadataService`, which keys by name and holds one member per name.

## Acceptance notes

- **Merged with `origin/main` in patch round 1** (`d64fc8e605`, a merge commit over `dc93781c19`). The 15 incoming commits touch nothing under `packages/rest`. The branch's delta against `origin/main` is still these 5 files, +357 / −3 (the changeset is now 23 lines), and `packages/spec` is byte-identical to `origin/main`'s.
- **The dispatcher's `/layers`, `/published` and `PUT` branches** declare no closed set either. Its `PUT` drops `?member=` (and, by its own settled ruling, `?force=`) exactly as `RestServer`'s did. These are the same family as #23072 but outside its population: the card names the dispatcher's item GET only. They are named in the report for the seat.
- The changeset grades `@objectstack/rest` `minor` under `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, with one ADR-0087 disposition (patch round 1, above). The claim's `patch` and bare `Clause-②: no` under-declared the narrowing. `@objectstack/runtime` is not in it, because no runtime file changed.
